# Independent audit of signed inverse arms for general profiles

PASS after independently deriving the kernels and reading `candidate fe4ccc381e7e406a` in full. I also rechecked its use of the audited local replacement theorem `candidate a260044e1f85011a`.

The source at zero may lie below the profile maximum. The two inverse arms are therefore signed, but this does not change the physical measure or require a projective reweighting. The theorem preserves a prescribed finite list of actual cap/coarea/moment records; it does not establish the remaining scalar interval inequality or OC.

## 1. Independent layer calculation

At a fixed positive level v, the shell contribution is the pair of point locations x=+v,-v with coefficient v^(m-1)/2. The continuous contribution is uniform on [-v,v] with coefficient (m-1)v^(m-2)/2. Their common axial interval is [-B(v),A(v)], even if one endpoint arm is negative.

Subtracting half the level volume, the signed cap density as a function of axial position z is

    sign(z) m v^(m-1)/2,                 |z|>s v,
    (m-1)v^(m-2) z/(2s),                 |z|<s v.

The shell accounts for the jumps at z=+/-s v. An even primitive is exactly

    j_s(t,v)=m v^(m-1)|t|/2             outside,
    j_s(t,v)=s(m+1)v^m/4
                +(m-1)v^(m-2)t^2/(4s) inside.

Continuity at either threshold fixes the constant in the inner expression. Integrating from -B to A gives j_s(A,v)-j_s(B,v), proving the cap formula without any assumption on the arm signs. Integrating the full level volume gives m v^(m-1)(A+B), with the coefficient in the source note.

## 2. Threshold derivatives and first moment

The derivative of j in its endpoint variable is the stated c_s, including its shell jumps. Its negative s times derivative in s is the stated even k_s: zero outside the strip, and

    -s(m+1)v^m/4+(m-1)v^(m-2)t^2/(4s)

inside. The formulas at the thresholds themselves need not be assigned for the integrals.

Each A(v)-s v is strictly decreasing. For the other threshold, if g(v)=A(v)+s v has a zero at x>0, concavity and g(0)>0 imply, for every y>x,

    g(y) <= -(y-x)g(0)/x <0.

Thus it has no second zero, including a zero interval. This is important: without the positive initial arm, a whole interval could sit at a derivative kink. Here each arm contributes at most two exceptional levels, a null set for dv.

The endpoint derivatives are bounded in absolute value by m v^(m-1)/2. On any compact positive-slope range, the slope derivatives are bounded by a constant times v^m, because the inner branch has |t|<=s v. These integrable bounds justify both differentiations under the level integral. Moving the threshold shifts the arms to A-epsilon and B+epsilon and yields C=int[c(A)+c(B)]. Differentiating with respect to s gives M=-sP'(s)=int[k(A)-k(B)]. This is also the direct coarea first moment, since on the cutting line sx=-z.

The cutting line passes through the interior source. It therefore cannot coincide with a supporting edge of the convex planar body, and no positive supporting-face contribution is lost by identifying this derivative with coarea. At m=1 the continuous layer is absent; the constant inner j and k formulas and the zero inner c formula remain correct.

## 3. Branch preservation under signed replacement

Partitioning at both signs of each selected slope and at each arm's zero is sufficient. A positive-threshold crossing is unique by strict decrease of A-sv. A negative-threshold crossing is unique by the preceding concavity inequality, and preserving its value makes every later value strictly negative. Before that crossing, concavity and the positive initial value keep the difference positive. If a negative-threshold crossing has not occurred internally, the old top value satisfies A(R)+sR>=0; increasing that completed top value preserves the same branch by concavity. The analogous statements for the zero threshold follow in the same way.

Consequently every kernel uses its original algebraic branch on each open partition cell. Outside-strip cap terms need integral v^(m-1)A, inside coarea terms need integral v^(m-2)A, and inside cap/moment terms need integral v^(m-2)A^2. The other terms depend only on fixed cell endpoints. These are exactly the three moments already preserved by the local theorem. The zero-slope cap formula uses the fixed arm signs and the same first-degree moment; preserving zero levels also preserves r(0), hence C(0).

## 4. Signed compactness, joins, and reconstruction

The local replacement proof does not require individual arm nonnegativity in its dual or contact argument. On an internal cell the fixed endpoint values give a uniform lower bound, while the fixed initial affine support gives a uniform upper bound. On the terminal cell the completed endpoint is no smaller than the original endpoint and the same affine support bounds it above. These bounds provide exactly the dominated-convergence control previously obtained from nonnegativity.

The original join-slope inequalities are unchanged. Hence both assembled arms remain continuous, concave, and nonincreasing. Their sum is concave, positive at level zero, and nonnegative at level R because each completed terminal value can only rise. Its nonnegativity at every intermediate level follows by the chord inequality. Thus the intervals [-Bhat(v),Ahat(v)] never reverse or disappear before the top.

The resulting compact set between these two arm graphs is convex and has nested level intervals. It is therefore the closed hypograph of a concave piecewise affine physical profile on the original axial interval. The preserved zero crossings retain the source height when it is below R; otherwise the retained top inequalities keep the source at height R. Initial arm values preserve both axial endpoints. No transformed density is substituted for the original planar component measure.

## 5. Statement precision

I requested that the profile hypothesis explicitly say continuous, or equivalently in this setting require its hypograph to be closed. Finite concavity alone permits a downward endpoint jump, which would not justify closed superlevel intervals. This continuity is automatic for the intended compact convex-body profile. With that clarification, no substantive gap remains in the signed-arm extension.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
